description: The system monitors vital signs such as heart rate, blood pressure, body temperature, oxygen saturation, sleep patterns, and stress levels using wearable sensors. It uses real-time data analysis and AI-based alerts to identify potential health risks, detect abnormalities, and provide early warnings to astronauts and mission control teams
summary: Building astronaut health-monitoring software requires designing a self-contained, user-friendly tool that lets non-physician crew members track physiological and behavioral indicators during deep-space missions.
details: Implement machine learning anomaly detection to flag subtle patterns before they escalate into medical emergencies, mirroring tools like the Canadian Space Agency Bio-Monitor and behavioral dashboards
